loText: Identify examples of wrong-way risk and examples of right-way risk.
question:
|  |  |
|---|---|
| Bank HJK has written puts on Bank PQR stock to a hedge fund and sold CDS |  |
| protection on Bank PQR to a manufacturer. Bank HJK and Bank PQR operate in |  |
| several of the same businesses and geographies and their performances are highly |  |
| correlated. Many in the market are concerned that rising interest rates could |  |
| negatively impact the credit quality of Bank HJK’s numerous borrowers, which in |  |
| turn would increase the credit spread of Bank HJK. From the perspectives of the |  |
| hedge fund and the manufacturer, which of the following is correct with respect to |  |
| their counterparty risk exposure to Bank HJK? |  |
| Hedge Fund | Manufacturer |
solution:
**Concept**

Wrong-way risk: exposure to a counterparty rises as that counterparty’s credit quality falls. Right-way risk is the opposite. Test each position by asking what happens to its value when the counterparty (Bank HJK) deteriorates.

**Exam trap.** Buying protection on an entity from a seller that is highly correlated with that entity is the textbook case of wrong-way risk: the protection is worth most exactly when the seller is least able to pay.

**Learning objectives tested:** CR-20l, CR-20k.
